parallel.requirements: Recognized the cleanroom obligation, no external source lookup, no wrapping, and the need to match `walk` CLI/TUI behavior by executing the bundled binary and docs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent spawned flags, TUI, and feature probes while continuing implementation itself; ownership remained shared in one /workspace rather than isolated per child.
parallel.implementation: Built a richer Go implementation with main.go, term.go, icons.go, statusbar.go, compile.sh, go.mod, an executable, and supporting docs/assets.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent and flags child both edited source in the same final workspace; final archive contained the rebuilt executable and core Go files but also git/docs/assets.
parallel.verification: Parallel ran local Go builds and behavior probes, including successful clean builds after statusbar changes, but official evaluation still failed 122 non-passed tests including skipped.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official result failed despite higher coverage than serial, and the source overwrite episode caused avoidable build and provenance churn around statusbar behavior.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same cleanroom reimplementation rules and explored required behavior through direct executable interaction and bundled documentation only.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned probing, implementation, revision, build, packaging, and closure without child handoffs or concurrent shared workspace edits.
serial.implementation: Implemented a Go version with main.go, tty.go, icons.go, statusbar.go, width.go, go.mod, compile.sh, and an executable after sequential probing.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial performed local file revisions and delivered a final tree, but the archive retained temporary probe directories, logs, and helper files alongside source.
serial.verification: Serial repaired build issues and reached a clean `go build`, but the official evaluator failed more behavior than parallel with 388 passed out of 786.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial artifact had lower evaluator coverage and included probe artifacts; those are ordinary single-agent defects rather than concurrency patterns.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the cleanroom reverse-engineering constraints and used executable/docs observations while dividing behavior discovery among children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same constraints and kept all probing and implementation in one trajectory with no delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No task identity difference exists; the difference is execution organization, with parallel covering more behavior but adding coordination risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spawned flags_probe, tui_probe, and feature_probe, then the parent kept implementing locally in the same workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial announced a standalone Go reimplementation and handled probing, implementation, and fixes itself.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had multi-agent overlap but weak file ownership for shared source; serial had slower but unambiguous ownership.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child and parent shared the same implementation context without a stable file/interface contract for `statusbar.go` ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial revised the same area locally, so the actor always had immediate access to current source state and did not require a cross-agent contract.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material context/interface gap was not a missing requirement in the child brief but the lack of isolated source ownership during live edits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced a broader Go implementation and iterated on status bar parsing, terminal behavior, icons, and final executable generation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also produced Go source but used a single-agent path and left more probe/test scaffolding in the final artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel implemented more evaluator-visible behavior, as reflected by score, but had concurrent statusbar replacement churn; serial was simpler and lower scoring.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent received child activity and continued work; no separate completed child implementation was proven ignored or unjoined outside the write episode.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle, so all results were local observations and local code revisions.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Lifecycle differences do not justify a retained join/timing label; the concrete adverse episode is shared-source replacement, not result retrieval.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent replaced statusbar.go wholesale, then the flags child later deleted and re-added the same source path after seeing replacement trouble.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial deleted and re-added statusbar.go as its own local revision, not as another agent overwriting live shared work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the retained concurrency-specific difference: parallel had cross-agent source overwrite; serial had ordinary single-actor revision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel obtained local clean builds after repairs but the completed official evaluator still failed the submitted solution.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial fixed compile errors and reached a clean local build, but the completed official evaluator failed with fewer passed tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on local build/behavior checks before closure; official outcome is both_fail, not a discordant pass/fail acceptance difference.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used child fan-out and consumed the run window, but still produced and packaged a higher-scoring failed artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out under the same outer limit with no child fan-out and delivered a lower-scoring artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Timeout and budget pressure are common terminal facts; they do not independently establish a load-imbalance label beyond the retained write churn.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current completed evaluations are not discordant: both solutions failed. Parallel solved more test cases than serial, plausibly because child probes and parent work covered more behavior, but the retained parallel Source Overwrite is only an adverse process episode and not an outcome-differential pass/fail explanation.
parallel_contributors: Parallel delegated flags, TUI, and feature probing while parent implemented, increasing behavioral coverage.
Parallel suffered a shared statusbar.go source overwrite episode that caused build and repair churn.
serial_contributors: Serial maintained single-actor ownership and avoided cross-agent overwrites.
Serial delivered lower evaluator coverage and retained probe artifacts in the archive.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel's final Go implementation covered more observed behavior than serial but still missed enough evaluator cases to fail.
Serial's final archive included temporary probe directories and helper logs, which are delivery/cleanup defects rather than concurrency errors.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no official outcome difference; supported comparative explanation only
